action: The Cyber Centre advises users and administrators to review the linked N-able bulletins and apply any necessary updates; the fixed versions it names are N-central 2026.4.1 HF3 and Patch Management 2.14.4.5829.
exec: Canada's Cyber Centre lists two N-central flaws in AV26-1165 and says nothing on whether either is being exploited.
plain: Canada's cyber agency published an advisory on N-able N-central naming two weaknesses, including one that lets someone bypass authentication on an appliance. It points users and administrators to N-able's updates.

key_findings: Affected: N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 and the N-central Patch Management Component before 2.14.4.5829.
CVE-2026-129271 is a local privilege escalation in N-central Patch Management.
CVE-2026-129272 is an authentication bypass on the MMS3 appliance through a predictable passcode.
The advisory makes no statement on whether either flaw is being exploited.
recommendations: Review the N-able advisories for CVE-2026-129271 and CVE-2026-129272 linked from the advisory.
Apply the necessary updates as they become available.
Check the N-able status page release notes for the fixed builds.

summary: Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1165 lists N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 and its Patch Management Component before 2.14.4.5829 as affected. It names two flaws: a local privilege escalation in Patch Management and an MMS3 appliance authentication bypass through a predictable passcode. The advisory does not say whether either is being exploited.
title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issues N-able N-central advisory AV26-1165

validation.note: The Cyber Centre advisory is the authority's own page; its RSS feed entry is the same publisher. CVE-2026-129272 was not found in NVD at the last check.
